REL.assert_all.null_law: false, null, unknown, and non-boolean predicate values fail
REL.assert_all.carrier_law: success preserves rows, values, identities, and order; failure is atomic

REL.assert_unique.null_law: null or missing key components fail
REL.assert_unique.carrier_law: canonical key tuples must be unique; success preserves the exact relation; failure is atomic

REL.select.reserved_field_law: reserved __* fields are not public column references

REL.where.null_law: three-valued unknown predicates are filtered out
REL.where.missing_field_law: missing predicate fields evaluate to unknown

REL.orderByStable.ordering_law: compare all explicitly supplied keys in their declared priority; rows equal on all keys retain their relative input order; no implicit valueCID or other tie-break key
REL.orderByStable.null_law: null placement is explicit per key and defaults to last
REL.orderByStable.empty_keys_law: empty keys preserve the exact input sequence, values and multiplicity
REL.orderByStable.compiler_boundary: candidate-key completion and its record belong to the compiler; the primitive receives completed explicit keys and does not infer keys or order evidence
REL.orderByStable.evidence_law: stability preserves an admitted input order but physical enumeration alone does not prove deterministic total order; empty sort preserves existing evidence and creates none

lean.scope: length only for an identity-function model; no key-order or runtime stability proof

REL.unnest.ordering_law: input order and array element order are preserved; null emits no rows and non-array values fail atomically

REL.dedupeRows.ordering_law: groups are ordered by the canonical typed key tuple: authored component order, NULLS FIRST per component, then the type-specific non-null order; the key CID is not an ordering key. Representative order is explicit and unresolved first-place ties fail

REL.topk.normalization_law: topk normalizes to orderByStable plus limit

REL.join.null_law: null or missing join keys never match
REL.join.ordering_law: left input order is primary and right matches preserve right input order; full join appends unmatched right rows in right input order

REL.groupBy.null_law: null group keys are first-class group key values

REL.derive.null_law: isnull is total over null and missing fields; cmp and bool null semantics follow the RelA evaluator
REL.derive.missing_field_law: missing derived-expression fields evaluate through the RelA evaluator
REL.derive.normalization_law: derived expressions evaluate against the input row only; aliases are mutually invisible; colliding aliases fail closed; output columns append aliases in declared exprs order
REL.derive.carrier_law: a predicate evaluated in scalar position maps three-valued unknown to null; the unknown sentinel never enters derived relation rows

REL.expression.normalize.expression_normalization_law: canonical expression normalization is idempotent and preserves evaluated truth/value for public LKv1 fixtures

REL.unionAll.ordering_law: inputs are concatenated in declared order and each input preserves its own row order

REL.window.sliding.ordering_law: each input row expands to containing windows in ascending window_start order

REL.window.project.ordering_law: window groups are ordered by window_start, window_end, then declared keys

REL.window.lag.ordering_law: lag reads a fixed offset inside deterministic partition order

REL.watermark.ordering_law: watermark labels preserve input row order and drop only rows marked late by the configured policy

REL.pivot.ordering_law: pivot columns are emitted in canonical string order

REL.unpivot.ordering_law: unpivot preserves row order and declared column order

REL.json.pick.null_law: null and missing object-key path segments produce null
REL.json.pick.carrier_law: the path carrier is an already-parsed object; stringified JSON, arrays, and scalar carriers fail atomically and are never parsed or coerced
